answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: Within 15 minutes. The operator must call MSHA at 1-800-746-1553 once the operator knows or should know that an accident involving a death has occurred.

claims.text: The operator must contact MSHA immediately, within 15 minutes, at the toll-free number once it knows or should know of an accident.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving:

claims.text: A death of an individual at the mine is one of the covered accidents.
claims.quote: (a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: Where no methane is present, the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent (with an increase of 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane only where methane is present).
claims.quote: the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: The device must be adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: Each operator must make available to each miner going underground an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: Underground mine evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months. Each drill must be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground.

claims.text: Underground mine evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held

claims.text: The drills must be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground.
claims.quote: Be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground;

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties (30 CFR 48.5). That training must be conducted in conditions that closely duplicate actual underground conditions, with approximately 8 hours given at the minesite.

claims.text: Each new miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

claims.text: The training must duplicate actual underground conditions as closely as practicable, with approximately 8 hours given at the minesite.
claims.quote: Such training shall be conducted in conditions which as closely as practicable duplicate actual underground conditions, and approximately 8 hours of training shall be given at the minesite.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 (8-hour time-weighted average) of 90 dBA, which is equivalent to a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard.

claims.text: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 of 90 dBA, equivalent to a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard.
claims.quote: Permissible exposure level. A TWA8 of 90 dBA or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: Berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway. This appears in both 30 CFR 57.9300 (underground metal and nonmetal mines) and 56.9300 (surface metal and nonmetal mines).

claims.text: Berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway (30 CFR 57.9300).
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

claims.text: The same height requirement appears in 30 CFR 56.9300.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: The breathable air must sustain each person for 96 hours. The rules also allow a refuge alternative to sustain persons for only 48 hours, but only if advance arrangements are made to supply additional supplies until rescue.

claims.text: The breathable air within the refuge alternative must sustain each person for 96 hours.
claims.quote: The breathable air sustains each person for 96 hours,

claims.text: A refuge alternative may sustain persons for only 48 hours if the ERP details advanced arrangements to provide additional supplies until rescue.
claims.quote: If the refuge alternative sustains persons for only 48 hours, the ERP shall detail advanced arrangements that have been made to assure that persons who cannot be rescued within 48 hours will receive additional supplies to sustain them until rescue.

answers.question: What must a written bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan contain under OSHA?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not address OSHA bloodborne pathogens exposure control plans. They cover only MSHA respiratory protection and respirable dust control plan rules.

answers.question: At what depth does OSHA require a construction trench to have a protective system such as shoring or a trench box?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not say at what depth OSHA requires a construction trench to have a protective system. They cover MSHA mine shaft and slope rules, not OSHA trenching rules.

answers.question: What FAA certification does a pilot need to fly a drone over a mine site?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not say what FAA certification a pilot needs to fly a drone over a mine site.

answers.question: When does a mine need an EPA stormwater discharge permit for runoff from its site?
answers.answer: The chunks don't say when a mine needs an EPA stormwater discharge permit. They cover impoundment design plans and permits for mining under water bodies. They don't mention EPA stormwater permits.
